chunks.content: 96 The Compliance Mistake That Could Tank Your Deal (and No One’s Talking About It) Hi Sara, Ever heard of Section 7216? No? Well, if you're in the business of buying or running an accounting firm, you probably should. I recently sat down with my colleague Tom Codevilla—our in-house privacy law whiz—and we dug into the legal landmine that is data compliance. This one’s especially for the folks planning to “buy a boring business” and then offshore all their labor while sipping cocktails. If that’s your plan... buckle up. Here’s the short version: Section 7216 is a federal regulation that applies to tax preparers. It requires informed, written consent from clients before you can share their data, even with your own contractors. That consent has to be in a specific format. Spoiler: your engagement letter with some 7216 language buried in the middle does not cut it. Even if 7216 doesn’t apply to you (because maybe you’re doing payroll or advisory work), don’t relax just yet. There’s an entire ecosystem of privacy laws that do apply. And no, “who’s going to know?” isn’t a great defense, especially when: A buyer is doing diligence, and your lack of compliance slashes your valuation A breach occurs, and you get hit with state-level notification requirements and expensive credit monitoring Your offshore contractor leaves a gaping security hole wide open, and your client data winds up floating on the dark web Yeah. Not ideal. What You Should Be Thinking About: Have you mapped how data enters, moves, and leaves your business? Do your third-party contractors have proper confidentiality agreements? Are you applying data minimization and least access principles? (Fancy terms for "don’t share more than you have to.") Are you training your team to spot phishing and social engineering scams? None of this is meant to scare you. (Okay, maybe just a little.) But this is the stuff buyers care about. It affects deal value, liability, and your ability to exit cleanly. Want to get ahead of it all? Watch the full episode on privacy pitfalls and how to protect your firm the smart way. It's a must-watch for anyone looking to buy, run, or eventually sell a business. And as always, if you like smart, slightly sarcastic legal advice from someone who reads purchase agreements for fun, subscribe to our YouTube channel, and check out DealAcademy.org.
